title: Diagram outline — search, dock and navigate

scenes.title: A deliberate editing routine
scenes.text: As a diagram grows, finding a task means searching a larger chart and more source. Diagram outline puts the elements in one searchable list. This example uses a small delivery plan. You can navigate without changing the source. Start with the View tab.

scenes.title: Find work by meaning
scenes.text: Open Outline from View, or find it through Commands. The list shows the diagram elements with their types and source lines. Type Design in the search field to narrow the list. The matching entry stays easy to identify. Searching itself leaves the plan unchanged.

scenes.title: Dock the outline and navigate a match
scenes.text: You can also keep the outline docked beside the diagram. Open it, search for Design, then choose Dock outline. Select the Design task from the filtered list to navigate to that element. The outline stays useful while you work through a larger document. One searchable view connects the diagram to its source.
